title: Production of The Aluminum Nitric-acid Keg (TANK) for Mitigating Explosions
author: Madelyn Miller
materials: A more detailed list of the necessary materials and equipment, including recommendations and alternatives, can be found in the "Materials" section. Materials Aluminum Blocks - 1 for Lid - 1 for Body 2 Alignment post rods 2 Folding chest handles and corresponding screws 2 Latches and corresponding screws Cutting fluid Optional: Placement guides (from the provided "Blueprint and Templates" PDF), printed to scale Equipment Drill bits meant for metal (at least 3/8", 7/16" and 1") Tap and die set Drill press Vise Wire brush 2 3/8" dowel centers Hydraulic press Center hole punch Belt sander 1" countersink drill bit

Before beginning drilling, adjust any materials as necessary. For example, it is sometimes difficult to find aluminum blocks in your required dimensions. Be sure your dimensions allow room on TANK's sides for the addition of handles and clasps. Cutting the aluminum block to size before drilling holes will save time, reduce weight, and decrease the likelihood of drilling holes in the incorrect locations. Additionally, alignment posts may need to be cut down to size. Image depicts cutting the aluminum blocks (lid and body clamped together) to our required length with a DoALL Horizontal Band Saw (Model C-916).

If you have the appropriate equipment and training, and do not wish to use screws, you can choose to weld the latches and handles on instead. With the lid on, place the parts of the latch on each side of TANK, ensuring there is some tension on the latch so the parts aren't too close to each other (the hook should attach to the lid and the loop to the body). Mark the screw holes with a marker. Alternatively, if you are using the recommended latches, you can use the included printout guide, but the guide should be employed as one piece with the lid sitting on the body to ensure the hook and latch are in line with one another. Then make a divot with a center hole punch or hammer and nail.

steps.title: Layout Ampule Wells
steps.instruction: Mark the center points for ampule wells on the body, ensuring no point is closer than 1.125" to the long edge, 1.25" to the short edge, or 1.25" from another center point.

substeps.instruction: Use a ruler and marker, marking gauge, or to-scale printout guide.
Create starting divots at each center point using a center-hole punch or hammer and nail.

steps.title: Drill Pilot Holes
steps.instruction: Secure the block to the drill press platform using a 6" cross slide vise (or heavy-duty clamps if the platform size allows and the clamp height permits a 5.5" drill travel).

substeps.instruction: Apply cutting fluid to the divots.
Drill pilot holes at each divot to a depth of 5.5" using a 3/8" to 1/2" bit at 700-1000 rpm.
Use a second person to sweep shavings/ribbons with a wire brush or dull knife and add cutting fluid as needed.
Periodically raise the bit to remove aluminum cuttings and cool the bit/block.
Clear holes of cuttings with compressed air while wearing eye protection.

steps.title: Drill Final Ampule Wells
steps.instruction: Drill each ampule well to its final size using a 1" drill bit at a speed of 250-400 rpm.

substeps.instruction: Slowly lower the drill bit into the pilot hole while the press is off to ensure perfect alignment without deflection.
Employ the same cutting fluid and shaving removal methods used for pilot holes.

steps.title: Chamfer and Finish Edges
steps.instruction: Remove sharp corners and edges from the ampule wells and the overall block.

substeps.instruction: Chamfer ampule well edges using a large countersink drill bit (in drill press or handheld) or a small chamfering bit in a handheld router.
Knock down remaining sharp edges/corners using a belt sander, file, or chamfering bit in a hand router.

steps.title: Prepare Lid Alignment Holes
steps.instruction: Mark and drill alignment post holes in the lid.

substeps.instruction: Measure 1/2" from each side on two opposite corners or use the printout guide to make starting divots with a center-hole punch or hammer and nail.
Using a cross slide vise and drill press, drill two holes to a depth of 3/4" using a 3/8" drill bit.

steps.title: Prepare Body Alignment Holes
steps.instruction: Create corresponding alignment holes in the body to match the lid.

substeps.instruction: Place dowel centers in the lid's post holes, align the lid flush with the body, and gently hammer the lid to create divots in the body (alternatively, use the printout guide).
Using a cross slide vise and drill press, drill two holes to a depth of 1.5" using a drill bit between 7/16" and 1/2".

steps.title: Install Alignment Posts
steps.instruction: Insert alignment posts into the lid.

substeps.instruction: Sand down the corners of the posts on a belt sander for easier insertion.
Use a hydraulic press to set the posts into the lid with a very tight fit; stop immediately once posts no longer travel to avoid mushrooming or deformation.
Place the lid on the body to ensure posts fit easily; redrill body holes larger if necessary.

steps.title: Install Latches and Handles
steps.instruction: Mount the hardware to the TANK sides.

substeps.instruction: Mark locations for latch and handle screws using a marker or printout guide; for handles, ensure the hinge sits at least halfway up when the lid is on.
Drill holes to a depth of 1/2" using a #36 bit for No. 6 screws and a #21 bit for No. 10 screws.
Tap the holes using cutting fluid (6-32 tap for No. 6 screws; 10-32 tap for No. 10 screws), keeping the tap perpendicular to the block.
Secure latches and handles with the appropriate screws.

steps.title: Clean and Prepare for Use
steps.instruction: Remove manufacturing residues from the ampule wells and alignment-post holes.

substeps.instruction: Clear holes with compressed air to remove aluminum shavings.
Scrub with water, a test tube brush, and a strong degreasing soap.
Rinse well and allow to dry thoroughly (do not use a combustion oven, as heating to 500°C may reduce material strength or undermine hardware integrity).

steps.title: Load and Run Oxidation
steps.instruction: Load the TANK with flame-sealed glass ampules containing samples and nitric acid.

substeps.instruction: Gently place ampules into wells (use long, large tweezers if helpful).
Place the lid on and secure it to the body with draw latches.
Transfer TANK to the oxidation oven and run the oxidation protocol (e.g., BPCA protocol).

steps.title: Unload and Post-Processing
steps.instruction: Recover samples and clean the device after oxidation.

substeps.instruction: Allow samples and TANK to return to room temperature.
Perform tasks in a fume hood wearing appropriate PPE (eye protection, gloves), assuming an explosion has occurred.
Remove the lid and extract ampules using large tweezers or by sliding soft tubing over the top for grip.
In case of explosion, remove all intact samples and neutralize any nitric acid before cleaning.
Tip TANK over to remove glass shards, then rinse with water and dry.
